notes: DOCUMENTED TARGET -- NOT RECORDABLE (daemon_capability: incapable; driver_capability: gap:no-interactive-driver). This spec states the arc the row asserts so a future re-assessment has something concrete to compare against; it is NOT expected to pass on junie as it stands, and it is deliberately not weakened to match what junie can do. THE ROW: a blocking dialog attached to NO tool call -- nothing carries the entry into waiting and nothing carries the release back out -- asserted on BOTH edges, plus a >=15s trailing idle that catches a session left pinned at waiting. Explicitly NOT tool-gate-permission-prompt (2-19) and NOT permission-gate-non-mutating-tool (2-26), both of which junie does satisfy through an open, approvable block. AGENT LAYER (satisfied -- 2 of the row's 4 triggers present in junie build 2929.5): PRESENT are the first-use workspace trust prompt (Screen$ProjectTrustScreen / ProjectTrustViewModel.onTrust / ProjectTrustViewKt, which carries the literal 'This project defines MCP servers that will be loaded once trusted:' and so covers the configured-server half of that trigger too; granting it writes ~/.junie/trust/<sha256>.json of kind EXACT_PROJECT, and one such artifact exists on the assessment host) and a product settings review (Screen$StatisticsConsentScreen + StatisticsConsentViewModel, backed by the persisted shareAnonymousStatistics key; also Screen$InvalidModelConfirmationScreen, Screen$ProjectOnboardingScreen, Screen$OnboardingModelScreen, Screen$ConfirmationScreen). ABSENT is a sandbox / network-access confirmation: /sandbox (Command$Sandbox) routes to TestViewKt$SandboxView, a developer playground, and a scan of every matterhorn class for 'network access' / 'Allow network' / 'internet access' yields only DefaultCommandSpecs' Gradle --offline description and GitPromptProvider's subagent prompt text -- junie has no sandbox model. NOT WIRED on the TUI path is MCP elicitation: the MCP Kotlin SDK ships CreateElicitationRequest and Client.setElicitationHandler, but no matterhorn class calls the setter; an ACP-path variant exists (AcpEvent$ElicitationRequest, JunieAgentSession$planDecider, FeedbackCommandKt$elicitationFlow) and is explicitly marked UNVERIFIED -- driving it needs an IDE acting as the ACP client, which this assessment did not do. TRANSPORT LAYER (why this cannot pass): Source is FilesUnderRoot{~/.junie/sessions, sessionIDFromPath}, and sessionIDFromPath mints a session ONLY from a file named exactly events.jsonl directly under a session-* directory. Every dialog above is a Screen in ej/app/cli/standalone/tui/app/state/Screen -- TUI application state raised by the CLI shell around the agent -- while SessionStore, the writer of events.jsonl, serializes only org.jetbrains.a2ux.api.AgentEvent / a2ux.extensions.A2uxEvent. There is no A2uxEvent for 'the trust screen is up'. The disk confirms it: on the assessment host, junie pid 82188 created sessions/session-260830-194006-s23k at 19:40:07 with transcript.md and NO events.jsonl, the trust file was written at 19:41:20, a DIFFERENT session id session-260830-194120-17p0 was created at 19:41:20, and its events.jsonl first appeared at 19:44:30 -- so for the ~73s the dialog blocked there was no file for the adapter to tail and no irrlicht session at all, and the session identity then changed across the grant so the block cannot even be paired with the session that eventually works. Every waiting rung in state_classifier.go is unreachable: the two hook-tier rungs because junie.Agent() declares no hooks (observe-only, one transcripts permission), transcript_permission_prompt (:152) because the junie parser sets TranscriptPermissionPending only from a SessionA2uxEvent under event.state=INPUT_REQUIRED, and user_blocking_tool / open_tool_stalled because both need an OPEN tool call -- which this row's premise excludes by definition. What a run would actually show is the INVERSION of the failure the trailing idle exists to catch: a proc-<PID> presession sitting at READY while the user stares at the modal. DRIVER LAYER: replaydata/agents/junie/ contains metadata.json and nothing else -- there is no driver-interactive.sh, so send/keys/wait_turn/sleep are all unimplemented for junie; and separately the trust trigger is launch-shaped rather than prompt-shaped (reached by launching into an untrusted cwd), which no existing driver primitive expresses. VACUOUS-PASS WARNING: junie CAN reach waiting -- through a genuine agent question (AskAsync/Choice under INPUT_REQUIRED, scenario 2-17) or a tool approval (2-19 / 2-26). Because the tool-less dialogs leave no trace at all, ANY waiting episode a future junie recording of THIS cell shows is by construction not the dialog this row is about; and this row's premise removes the open-tool evidence that could otherwise cross-check it. Never accept a waiting episode here without naming which Screen produced it and which events.jsonl line carried it. SESSION IDENTITY: junie writes events.jsonl only when the first TASK starts, while the CommandPattern matcher binds the process at launch, so a proc-<PID> presession is expected first and the real session (id = the session-* directory name) only afterwards. The birth is therefore modelled in two phases and every later phase anchors to the REAL session, never the presession row. This shape is INFERRED from the adapter plus the on-disk timeline above -- junie has 0 recordings -- and is the first thing to correct if this row ever becomes recordable.

text: The proc-<PID> presession appears in ready once the junie process is matched at launch.
The real session appears when ~/.junie/sessions/<session-id>/events.jsonl is first written, whose first line is a UserPromptEvent -- so for junie the real session is born already working.

The tool-less dialog opens (ProjectTrustScreen, or StatisticsConsentScreen) and the session goes working -> waiting with NO tool call in flight. The entry edge is carried by nothing: no tool_use opened, and none will complete to end it. Allow up to 15s, since some agents publish this signal on a timer. UNREACHABLE ON JUNIE TODAY: no line is written to events.jsonl on this edge, and during the trust dialog no events.jsonl exists at all.

The user answers the dialog; the session resumes waiting -> working. The release edge is likewise carried by nothing -- no tool result closes it. UNREACHABLE ON JUNIE TODAY: answering the trust screen mints a NEW session id, so even a reconstruction could not pair this edge with the entry.
The turn finishes back to ready -- full arc ready -> working -> waiting -> working -> ready. On junie the boundary would be TaskState.

THE LOAD-BEARING PHASE. The session is still ready after a >=15s trailing idle: it does not fall back to waiting, and it was not left pinned at waiting from the dialog onward by something no later event retires. Junie's failure mode is the inversion -- pinned at READY throughout the dialog -- which this phase alone cannot distinguish from a pass, which is exactly why dialog_waiting above is the phase that must go red.
A single process_exited on the session at TUI teardown; the live state immediately before teardown is ready.
